name: cedar-on-hook-test
_note: Isolated live proof of the live-guard Cedar PreToolUse hook, run on BOTH engines. Four agent legs share one check, as two matched lanes: `allow`/`deny` on claude-sonnet-4-6 and `allow-codex`/`deny-codex` on codex gpt-5.5. An allow leg makes only permitted calls and is expected GREEN; a deny leg is instructed to attempt a forbidden call, the hook refuses it, and the leg is expected RED via on_fail:block (a denied call is not a form defect to retry, so it never iterates; no leg declares on_blocked so the run keeps flowing). One green + one red PER LANE IS the pass condition -- two greens in a lane means the guard never fired there, two reds means it over-blocks. The lanes differ in three engine-specific ways, all forced by measurement (docs/STATUS.md, 'live-guard on codex'): codex pins version 0.147.0 because gh-aw's default 0.135.0 dispatches no hooks at all; it registers the hook via `-c` on the command line because gh-aw truncates $CODEX_HOME/config.toml after pre-agent-steps; and it must NOT set CEDAR_LIVE_GUARD_ON_DENY=stop, which fails OPEN on codex. `record` is a DISPATCHED code node because an inline hook's return is reduced to {conclusion,summary} and could not carry a ledger; it reduces the fork with from_fork and publishes all legs' guard events as evidence. Trigger /cedar-hook on a PR comment.

states.label: record (ledger of both legs' guard events)
